system.name: SS 433
system.description: A spectacular microquasar 17,900 light-years away in Aquila — a black hole devouring a companion supergiant and firing twin jets of plasma at a quarter of the speed of light in opposite directions. It was the first object discovered to have relativistic jets, making it a landmark in high-energy astrophysics.

ss433.name: SS 433 (Black Hole)
ss433.description: A stellar-mass black hole of roughly 10.8 solar masses at the heart of the SS 433 X-ray binary. It accretes material from its companion at a supercritical rate, launching two narrow jets of plasma in opposite directions at 0.26 times the speed of light — tilted 20° from the orbital axis and precessing like a spinning top on a 162.5-day cycle.
ss433.funFact: SS 433's precessing jets drew double-helix patterns of X-ray-emitting plasma across 300 light-years inside the supernova remnant W50 — making it look like a cosmic corkscrew when viewed in radio and X-ray light.

ss433companion.name: SS 433 Companion
ss433companion.description: An evolved A-type supergiant overflowing its Roche lobe and dumping material onto the black hole at several times the Eddington limit. This supercritical accretion rate is what drives the relativistic jet outflows — material that cannot fall onto the black hole fast enough is instead launched as collimated plasma streams at 0.26c.
ss433companion.funFact: The companion's orbital motion causes the jet emission lines to Doppler shift on a 13-day cycle — allowing astronomers to map the binary orbit entirely from spectroscopy, even though the system is hidden behind tens of thousands of light-years of dust.
